clue.text: Moab as revealed by Spooner's high-class, eh?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words here trade their starts by sound

parts.note: posh means upmarket or high-class
what? and eh? are both ways of asking someone to repeat themselves

explanation.surface: A puzzled query about the biblical land of Moab, as some upper-crust speaker might phrase it.
explanation.walkthrough: Spooner's swap turns POSH WHAT into 'wash pot' by sound. The definition is a quotation: Psalm 60 says 'Moab is my washpot'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Psalms God calls Moab his basin for washing, a biblical image of a subdued land.

clue.text: Half of all adults were victorious, this person included

indicators.note: included means the self-reference sits inside the word for winning

parts.note: won means were victorious
the setter referring to themself gives me

explanation.surface: A boast that half the grown-ups won, the speaker among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Roughly half of the adult population is female, so the phrase describes that group.

clue.text: Tot eats food item sitting up in rocky bed

indicators.note: eats means the total word takes the food inside it

parts.note: to tot up is to add, and a tot is a sum

indicators.note: in a down entry, sitting up means the word for the pastry is read bottom to top

parts.note: a tart is a pastry food item

explanation.surface: A toddler munching a snack while propped up in a stony bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a small child, but here it means adding up. 'sitting up' turns the pastry word round, as this is a down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Geologists call a layer of rock a stratum, a bed in the rock sequence.

clue.text: Stroke little cherub, showing no love

indicators.note: showing no means the round letter for love is removed from the cherub

parts.note: a putto is a small cherub figure in Renaissance art
love is zero in tennis, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone petting a little angel figure without any affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' looks like a caress but is the golf shot. PUTTO loses its O.
explanation.definitionFit: On the green a golfer's gentle shot toward the hole is one stroke.

clue.text: According to mood, modify account having secured the last word

parts.note: to temper is to modify or moderate
amen is the word that ends a prayer
a tally is a running account or count

explanation.surface: An instruction to adjust a bill depending on how one feels, once the final say is in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having secured' says the account word holds the prayer's closing word. 'Amen' is the conventional last word because it ends a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something by disposition or temper is acting in line with one's mood.

clue.text: Hangs around in dances slowly beginning to get going

indicators.note: the opening letter is sent away, so the first letter of the dance word goes

parts.note: to smooch is to dance slowly in a close embrace

explanation.surface: Someone loitering at a slow dance before finally making a move.
explanation.definitionFit: To loiter aimlessly in a place is to mooch, a British informal verb.

clue.text: What an iPod can offer is very pleasing

definitions.meaning: an iPod plays songs through headphones straight into the listener
an idiom for news that is delightful to hear

explanation.definitionFit: Literally a music player delivers tunes; figuratively the idiom means welcome, delightful news.

clue.text: What badly stocked builders' merchant may be in the yard?

definitions.text: What badly stocked builders' merchant may be
definitions.meaning: a supplier with no doors left to sell has run out of them
outside, in the open air rather than indoors

explanation.definitionFit: Being outside the house means outdoors; a shop lacking stock of doors is literally without them.

clue.text: Bit of a buzz comes with the raising of certain skeletal component

parts.note: a hum is a low buzzing sound

indicators.note: in a down entry, raising means the word for certain is read upward

parts.note: sure means certain

explanation.surface: A buzzing noise accompanies the lifting of some bone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the raising of' reverses the word for certain, since this is a down entry and raising reads it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper arm bone is a single part of the human skeleton.

clue.text: Grass a problem in the mouth, might you say?

indicators.note: might you say signals that the words are spoken aloud to give the answer's sound

parts.note: a sore gum is a painful dental complaint

explanation.surface: Is grass a cause of mouth trouble, someone wonders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grass' could be the informant, but here it is the cereal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorghum is a tall cereal plant of the grass family, grown for grain and fodder.

clue.text: When St David is celebrated by group of provinces

parts.note: St David's Day, the Welsh national day, is 1 March, written as MAR plus I for one
by as in multiplication, three by four, means times

explanation.surface: A festive date noted alongside some regional grouping.
explanation.walkthrough: MAR I is 1 March, St David's Day. The definition is Canada's Maritime Provinces.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada's three Atlantic coastal provinces are known collectively by this name.

clue.text: One could show minutes into game, right?

definitions.text: One could show minutes into game, right?

indicators.note: into means the abbreviation for minutes goes inside the word for a match

parts.note: a tie is a game or match, as in a cup tie

explanation.surface: Asking whether a gadget could display how far through a match we are.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: a clock showing how many minutes a game has run.
explanation.definitionFit: A clock device measuring elapsed time displays how long a match has been running.

clue.text: Like some financial figures — caught editor out

indicators.note: out means the editor's abbreviation is dropped from the catching word

parts.note: netted means caught, as fish in a net

explanation.surface: Financial figures snared, with the editor left out of the reporting.
explanation.definitionFit: Profits after deductions are described with this British spelling of the word for after-tax totals.

clue.text: So unhappy to have just missed podium, not seen as superior looking ahead

parts.note: hence means so or therefore

indicators.note: not seen means the letter for superior is left out of the place word

parts.words: unhappy to have just missed podium
parts.note: finishing fourth means just missing the top three on the podium
U stands for upper class, socially superior

explanation.surface: An athlete gloomy at narrowly missing a medal, but with an eye to the future.
explanation.walkthrough: U means upper class; FOURTH without it is FORTH.
explanation.definitionFit: From now on describes time going forward, so it fits facing the future.

clue.text: Deer prints seen around — bad news for cattle?

indicators.note: around signals the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: Hoof marks of deer spotted nearby, which could spell trouble for the herd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' signals the rearranging of DEER PRINTS.
explanation.definitionFit: Cattle plague was a deadly viral disease of livestock, eradicated in 2011.

clue.text: "I ___', says educated girl, living for ever

parts.note: the blank completes the phrase I am
Rita is the heroine of the play and film Educating Rita

explanation.surface: A schooled young woman announcing herself as immortal.
explanation.walkthrough: Educating Rita is a Willy Russell play about a hairdresser who takes up studying.
explanation.definitionFit: In Hindu myth this drink of the gods confers immortality, and the word also means deathlessness.

clue.text: Animal getting round cat writer, not old

parts.note: a round shape is the letter O

indicators.note: not means the word for old is taken away from the writer's name

parts.note: T S Eliot wrote Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats, Old Possum being his nickname
taken as written

explanation.surface: A creature circling the author of cat poems, the young version of him.
explanation.definitionFit: This American marsupial is a creature known for playing dead.

clue.text: Get killed on the run? Thankfully he didn't!

definitions.text: Get killed on the run? Thankfully he didn't!

indicators.note: on means the dying word follows the running word

parts.note: a rush is a run or a dash
to die is to get killed

explanation.surface: A writer in hiding could have been murdered while running, and happily was not.
explanation.walkthrough: The novelist lived under a fatwa for years after The Satanic Verses; the whole clue describes him.
explanation.definitionFit: The author of The Satanic Verses went into hiding under a death threat and survived.

clue.text: Regrets key being jammed — gets out after trouble?

indicators.note: being jammed means the key is squeezed inside the regretting word

parts.note: rues means regrets
Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: Someone sorry that a key has stuck, wondering how to get it free.
explanation.definitionFit: Saving someone means getting them out of danger or difficulty.

clue.text: Carmela, perhaps, as a noted female

definitions.meaning: Carmela is the wife of Tony in the TV drama The ...
a woman with the highest singing voice, noted as in singing notes

explanation.surface: Carmela described as a well-known woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Carmela's surname in the TV series, and the highest female voice, singing notes.

clue.text: Society managed to rebuff drugs agents

indicators.note: to rebuff is to send back, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: ran means managed, as in ran a business

explanation.surface: A club organised a snub to narcotics officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rebuff' turns SOCRAN round to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Narcotics officers, in US slang, are agents fighting drug crime.

clue.text: An ogre's destroyed due to stone-hurlers

indicators.note: destroyed means the letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: An ogre was brought down by people throwing rocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Onagers were ancient siege catapults that flung rocks.

clue.text: A miser's apt to become perverse, not joining in

indicators.note: becoming perverse means turning awry, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Stinginess tends to turn a person contrary and unsociable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to become perverse' rearranges A MISERS APT.
explanation.definitionFit: A policy of breaking away and keeping apart is the opposite of uniting with others.

clue.text: Wheeled carriage beginning to move when this is provided?

definitions.text: Wheeled carriage beginning to move when this is provided?

indicators.note: the first letter is shifted to a new place, here the end

parts.note: a pram is a wheeled baby carriage

explanation.surface: A buggy can get going only once a slope is supplied.
explanation.walkthrough: PRAM's opening P goes to the back. The whole clue describes a slope letting a pram roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A sloping access lets a pushchair get up or down steps.

clue.text: Asian city god wanting American investment

indicators.note: investment means clothing or enclosing, so the god surrounds the American letters

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of the wild

explanation.surface: A deity in an Asian city seeks money from the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' is used in its old sense of clothing or besieging.
explanation.definitionFit: Pusan is the older romanised name of Busan, South Korea's major port city.

clue.text: Determined to show concern

definitions.meaning: resolute and unwavering, as in a resolute stance
a business or company, as in a going concern

explanation.definitionFit: A resolute person is unyielding; a business company is also called by this name.

clue.text: Edict that puts our country at sea, confused

parts.note: UK, the United Kingdom, is the setter's home country

indicators.note: confused means the letters are muddled up

explanation.surface: A decree that leaves Britain all at sea and baffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' looks like the anagram signal, but 'confused' rearranges SEA into ASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A ukase was a decree issued by the Russian tsar, so any arbitrary order.

clue.text: See, when going round pits, quality of soil

parts.note: lo is an old word for see or behold

indicators.note: going round means the word for when is placed around the pits

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
mines are pits, as in coal pits

explanation.surface: Look at a site passing old mine workings and note the earth's character.
explanation.definitionFit: Soil rich in clay, sand and humus has this crumbly fertile character.

clue.text: Roguish ticket seller being seized in robust manner

indicators.note: being seized means the seller is caught inside the crafty word

parts.note: sly means roguish or cunning
a tout sells tickets unofficially at inflated prices

explanation.surface: A dodgy ticket hawker grabbed firmly by the police.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something vigorously and sturdily is the adverbial sense of strong and robust.

clue.text: Foolish American boy, who makes you think of Wallis?

definitions.text: who makes you think of Wallis?

parts.note: simp is American slang for a fool
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A daft American lad, presumably Bart, called to mind by a famous name.
explanation.walkthrough: Wallis Simpson married Edward VIII after his abdication; the surface also hints at Bart, the cartoon boy.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname recalls Wallis, the American divorcee whose marriage led to a king's abdication.
